q-39096.name: Question 1
q-39096.problem: An arithmetic series has ${a}_{3}=-16$ and ${a}_{8}=-51,$ where ${a}_{3}$ and ${a}_{8}$ are the third and eighth terms of the series, respectively. What is the sum of the first $10$ terms of the series, expressed using sigma notation?
q-39096.worked_solution:
Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{8}-{a}_{3}}{8-3} \\  & =\frac{-51-(-16)}{5} \\  & =\frac{-35}{5} \\  & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

As ${a}_{3}=-16$, using the formula for the $n$th term, we can compute ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ -16 & ={a}_{1}+(3-1)(-7) \\ -16 & ={a}_{1}-14 \\ {a}_{1} & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So we have ${a}_{1}=-2$ and $d=-7.$ Thus, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-2+(n-1)(-7) \\  & =-2-7n+7 \\  & =-7n+5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the first ten terms can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{10}(-7n+5)\end{aligned}
$$

q-39096.html:
Question 1
?

An arithmetic series has a3=−16 and a8=−51, where a3 and a8 are the third and eighth terms of the series, respectively. What is the sum of the first 10 terms of the series, expressed using sigma notation?

a
∑n=110(−7n+5)
b
∑n=110(5n+1)
c
∑n=110(−6n+2)
d
∑n=110(−2n−10)
e
∑n=110(−8n+8)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference:

d=a8−a38−3=−51−(−16)5=−355=−7

As a3=−16, using the formula for the nth term, we can compute a1, as follows:

an=a1+(n−1)d−16=a1+(3−1)(−7)−16=a1−14a1=−2

So we have a1=−2 and d=−7. Thus, the formula for the nth term is:

an=−2+(n−1)(−7)=−2−7n+7=−7n+5

Therefore, the sum of the first ten terms can be written as:

∑n=110(−7n+5)

q-67199.name: Question 2
q-67199.problem:
Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

$$
-12-7-2+3+8+…+28+33
$$
q-67199.worked_solution:
The first term ${a}_{1}=-12$ and the common difference is:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =-7-(-12) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =-12+(n-1)(5) \\  & =-12+5n-5 \\  & =5n-17\end{aligned}
$$

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =33 \\ 5n-17 & =33 \\ 5n & =33+17 \\ 5n & =50 \\ n & =10\end{aligned}
$$

There are $10$ terms in total, from $n=1$ to $n=10.$ So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{10}(5n-17)
$$

q-67199.html:
Question 2
?

Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

−12−7−2+3+8+…+28+33

a
∑n=110(5n−12)
b
∑n=110(5n−17)
c
∑n=110(12−5n)
d
∑n=09(5n−17)
e
∑n=133(−5n+17)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The first term a1=−12 and the common difference is:

d=a2−a1=−7−(−12)=5

Hence, the formula for the nth term is:

an=a1+(n−1)d=−12+(n−1)(5)=−12+5n−5=5n−17

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the nth term:

an=335n−17=335n=33+175n=50n=10

There are 10 terms in total, from n=1 to n=10. So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

∑n=110(5n−17)

q-107663.name: Question 3
q-107663.problem:
Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

$$
1+\frac{5}{3}+\frac{7}{3}+…+\frac{37}{3}+13
$$
q-107663.worked_solution:
The first term ${a}_{1}=1$ and the common difference is:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}-1 \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =1+(n-1)(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =1+\frac{2}{3}n-\frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}n+\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =13 \\ \frac{2}{3}n+\frac{1}{3} & =13 \\ \frac{2}{3}n & =\frac{38}{3} \\ n & =19\end{aligned}
$$

There are $19$ terms in total, from $n=1$ to $n=19.$ So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{19}(\frac{2}{3}n+\frac{1}{3})
$$

Question 3
?

Express the following arithmetic series using sigma notation.

1+53+73+…+373+13

a
∑n=119(53n+13)
b
∑n=119(23n+13)
c
∑n=119(53n+1)
d
∑n=119(23n+1)
e
∑n=119(23n+43)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The first term a1=1 and the common difference is:

d=a2−a1=53−1=23

Hence, the formula for the nth term is:

an=a1+(n−1)d=1+(n−1)(23)=1+23n−23=23n+13

We don't know the index of the last term, but we can find it using the formula for the nth term:

an=1323n+13=1323n=383n=19

There are 19 terms in total, from n=1 to n=19. So, the sigma notation for the given sum is:

∑n=119(23n+13)
